'''''Neoblechnum''''' is a [[genus]] of [[fern]]s in the family [[Blechnaceae]], subfamily Blechnoideae, with a single species '''''Neoblechnum brasiliense''''', according to the [[Pteridophyte Phylogeny Group]] classification of 2016 (PPG I).<ref name=PPGI/> The genus is accepted in a 2016 classification of the family Blechnaceae,<ref name=GaspDittSmitSali16/> but other sources sink it into a very broadly defined ''Blechnum'', equivalent to the whole of the PPG I subfamily;<ref name=ChriChas14/> the species is then known as '''''Blechnum brasiliense'''''. It is called '''Brazilian dwarf tree fern''', '''red Brazilian tree fern''', and '''red dwarf tree fern'''.<ref name="grin">{{GRIN|id=312588|name=''Blechnum brasiliense'' Desv.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Plant database entry for Red Dwarf Tree Fern (Neoblechnum brasiliense) with 18 images and 13 data details. |url=https://garden.org/plants/view/114152/Red-Dwarf-Tree-Fern-Neoblechnum-brasiliense/ |website=garden.org}}</ref>

==Description==
The erect rhizome of ''Neoblechnum brasiliense'' forms a thin stipe-stubbed trunk up to {{convert|30|cm|in}} in height. The new foliage is a striking deep red color. As the fronds mature it turns to a glossy green.<ref name=forestferns/> On some selections, the new fronds emerge a pinkish-red.

==Distribution==
The fern is native to the warm and humid subtropical forests of South America.<ref name="forestferns">{{Cite web |title=Forest Ferns.uk: cultivation of ''Blechnum brasiliense'' |url=http://www.forestferns.co.uk/tree-ferns/blechnum/blechnum-brasiliense |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160427030614/http://www.forestferns.co.uk/tree-ferns/blechnum/blechnum-brasiliense |archive-date=2016-04-27 |access-date=2016-09-06}}</ref>

Habitats include:<ref name=grin/>
* the [[Atlantic Forest|Atlantic Forest biome]], within southeastern [[Brazil]], [[Uruguay]], and the interiors of [[Argentina]] and [[Paraguay]].  
* the [[Amazon region]], in Brazil, Peru, Bolivia, [[Colombia]], [[Ecuador]], Venezuela, and [[Guyana]].
* [[Guatemala]].

==Cultivation==
''Neoblechnum brasiliense'' is cultivated as an [[ornamental plant]].<ref name=forestferns/> In the [[United Kingdom|UK]] (under the synonym ''Blechnum brasiliense'') it has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name="RHSPF">{{cite web |title=RHS Plantfinder - ''Blechnum brasiliense'' |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/21330/i-Blechnum-brasiliense-i/Details |accessdate=12 January 2018}}</ref> 
As it will not tolerate temperatures below {{convert|15|C|F}} it must be grown under glass all year in temperate regions.

===Cultivars===
Named [[cultivar]]s include:
* 'Crispum' — segments have prominently crisped margins<ref name=forestferns/><ref>{{cite web |title=Longwood Gardens Plant Explorer — ''Blechnum brasiliense'' 'Crispum' |url=http://plantexplorer.longwoodgardens.org/weboi/oecgi2.exe/INET_ECM_DispPl?NAMENUM=2407&DETAIL=1 |website=Longwoodgardens.org}}</ref>
* 'Cristatum' — segments are crested<ref name=forestferns/>
* 'Volcano' — red dwarf tree fern, new foliage is red<ref>{{Cite web |title=Blechnum brasiliense 'Volcano' plants |url=https://www.thompson-morgan.com/p/blechnum-brasiliense-volcano/t62540TM |website=www.thompson-morgan.com}}</ref>
